name: npy-viewer
description: View NumPy .npy files in VS Code — as images, heatmaps, contact sheets, plots and exact values, alongside full descriptive statistics. Recognises RGB, channel-first and batched image tensors from the array shape, opens files larger than memory, and needs no Python.

untrustedWorkspaces.description: Arrays are parsed and rendered normally — reading a .npy file executes no code from the workspace. The optional Python/NumPy backend is not started in an untrusted workspace, because it launches an interpreter.

virtualWorkspaces.description: Arrays are streamed directly from disk so that files larger than memory can be opened, which needs real filesystem access.

npyViewer.python.enabled.markdownDescription:
Analyse arrays with a Python + NumPy subprocess when an interpreter is available. NumPy reads every dtype, including pickled object arrays, and computes exact quantiles on arrays too large for the built-in parser to hold in memory. When disabled — or when no interpreter is found — the built-in TypeScript parser is used instead; it needs no Python and is comparably fast on ordinary numeric arrays.

This setting is machine-scoped: a workspace cannot turn the subprocess on for you.

npyViewer.python.path.markdownDescription:
Absolute path to the Python interpreter used for parsing. Leave empty to auto-detect (the Python extension's selected interpreter is preferred, then `python3` / `python` / `py` on `PATH`).

This setting is machine-scoped and can only be set in your user or remote settings. A folder you open must never be able to choose which executable this extension launches.

npyViewer.python.showInstallHint.description: Show a dismissible hint recommending Python + NumPy when the extension falls back to the built-in parser.

npyViewer.preview.maxElements.description: Maximum number of array elements sent to the view. Larger arrays are decimated for display; statistics are still computed over every element.

npyViewer.preview.imageMaxSide.description: Longest edge, in pixels, of a rendered image preview. Larger images are downscaled.

npyViewer.stats.exactPercentileLimit.markdownDescription:
Element count up to which percentiles and the median are computed exactly. Above this they are estimated from a uniform random sample and labelled *approximate*. Counts, extrema, mean and standard deviation are always exact over every element, whatever this is set to.

The sample is held in memory at 8 bytes per element, so raising this costs roughly 8 MB per million. Sampling error on the median is negligible well below the default.

npyViewer.stats.histogramBins.description: Number of bins in the distribution histogram.

npyViewer.view.colormap.description: Default colormap used for heatmaps and single-channel image previews.

npyViewer.view.autoNormalize.markdownDescription: Stretch float image data to the full display range using the array's own min/max. Disable to clamp to the dtype's natural range (`0..1` for floats, `0..255` for `uint8`).

scripts.compile: npm run check-types && npm run lint && node esbuild.js
scripts.package: npm run check-types && npm run lint && node esbuild.js --production
scripts.pretest: npm run compile-tests && npm run compile && npm run lint
